question.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $C?$

I. $B∨(B∧C)$

II. $(B∧C)∨C$

III. $(C∧B)∧C$
question.worked_solution:
The law that disjunction absorbs conjunction is stated as

$$
C∨(C∧B)≡C.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is *not* logically equivalent to $C.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}B∨(B∧C) & ≡B≢C.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is logically equivalent to $C.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(B∧C)∨C & ≡C∨(B∧C) \\  & ≡C∨(C∧B) \\  & ≡C.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is *not* logically equivalent to $C.$ This statement cannot be simplified using the absorption laws.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
